text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Several new Volvo models are on the way, but the investments are likely to be outside Sweden, such as in Asia, so no new jobs in Sweden will result.

- Saab Automobile head Robert Hendry said the company's ambition to increase car sales by 50 percent would mean more jobs but does not rule out the possibility of new production taking place outside Sweden.
- Few parents are interested in taking part in policymaking at their children's schools although they now have the opportunity to do so.
- Over the past five years, companies controlled by business magnate Jan Stenbeck have been involved in no less than 140 legal disputes in Stockholm courts alone.
"Jan Stenback has brought to Sweden the U.S. tradition of more legal actions in business," a spokesman for Stenbeck-controlled media group Kinnevik said.
- Stockmarket speculation and opening a business are the top ways to make money, a survey of entrepreneurs says.
